briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is recorded in my own words before I read the brief. The brief asks for a work that 'barely acknowledges the market at all', where the market registers 'only faintly', with 'nothing that a casual viewer would notice at thumbnail size', and it closes with the explicit instruction 'Do not manufacture drama'. My Stage 1 description, written blind, says the state change is 'large, monotone in one direction, and legible without comparison' and that at 120px 'the state axis survives completely -- the stress row is instantly dimmer, smaller and simpler and the recovery row instantly brighter and larger, with no need to compare tiles'. That is the exact inverse of the commission, and it is the loudest fact about the sheets. 9548 neutral has three budding satellite arms; 9548 stress has none at all -- not a tightened enclosure, an amputation. 9369 collapses from a large disc with a three-body moon chain to a small disc with a dot. Every recovery tile overshoots its own neutral in both size and saturation to a bright lemon gold. Secondly, the brief names its subject as 'concentric enclosure, one boundary inside another, with a small dense centre held at the middle', and says the variation between tokens is 'the number of enclosures and the character of the centre they hold'. The concentric stacking is genuinely there, but the centre is usually not small and not dense: in 9011, 10622, 10980 and 9548 the middle is a large inert flat cocoa field occupying most of the figure, and the actual variation between tokens runs on a different axis entirely -- silhouette family and radiating limbs (9727's three sprawling arms, 9906's two, 9548's three) which are not enclosures at all. The palette instruction is the one clause fully honoured. Because briefFidelity is the gate, the verdict cannot be PASS.
composition: Centred and concentric as asked, but the focal hierarchy is inverted against the brief's own subject. The brightest, highest-contrast material sits at the OUTER fringe, where the translucent petals overlap least, while the centre -- the thing the brief says is held -- is the dullest, flattest region of the frame. The eye is therefore pulled outward, away from the middle. 9190 is the one tile that gets it right: a genuinely small dark square nested inside a square inside a star, with the middle winning. 10443 also holds, being sparse enough that the diamond reads as an object in space. Against that, 9011, 10622 and 10980 are a large brown mass with decoration only at the rim, and 9727 has no centre worth holding at all -- it is limbs with a small core between them. The brief asks that 'most of the frame' be given to the dark; 10264, 10801, 10980 and both recovery tiles of 9011 and 9190 fill the frame edge to edge instead, so the dark stops being the subject and becomes a thin surround.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis by a distance, and I said so before reading the brief. All twelve share one hue family, one near-black ground, one construction logic (translucent regular shapes stacked on a common centre so alpha accumulation does all the tonal work), and one centred placement. Nothing here reads as a stray. Even the outliers stay in the family: 9369's disc-and-moon-chain, 10443's near-empty diamond and 10264's dense gold burst are recognisably built by the same hand from the same parts. Laid out on the contact sheet this is one project and could not be mistaken for a folder of unrelated tokens. If the collection shipped, coherence would not be the reason anyone doubted it.
palette: Chosen, and the one clause of the brief delivered without qualification: gold and amber over deep ink, with umber appearing exactly where the translucent fills pile up, so the colour range is produced by the construction rather than picked from a list. The contrast range does real work -- accumulation reads as depth and weight, which suits 'settled and permanent'. Two reservations. 10085 is pitched so close to the ground that the hexagon and its square barely separate from the black at 256px and read as an almost blank rectangle at 120px, which is not restraint but under-exposure. And the recovery row (9011, 9190, 9548 recovery, plus 10264 at neutral) pushes to a bright near-lemon that is louder than 'gold and umber over deep ink' and is part of how the state drama gets manufactured.
seedVariation: There is real variation and it is not one work at twelve rotations -- the silhouette families are genuinely distinct: round 9369, square 9190/10801/10622, hexagonal 10085, diamond 10443, star 9011/10980, limbed 9548/9727/9906, burst 10264. The problem is that the variation runs on an axis the brief did not commission and is thin on the axis it did. The brief says what varies is 'the number of enclosures and the character of the centre they hold'; the centres are the most similar thing in the set, a repeated flat brown field, while the loudest differentiator is the presence and sprawl of radiating limbs. In the other direction the spread also overreaches at the top end: 9727, with three long asymmetric arms breaking toward three corners, and 10264, a dense frame-filling gold burst, do not read as siblings of 10443's quiet diamond under a rubric of 'still, contemplative, settled, unhurried'. They are not different projects, but they are a wider register than the brief's own word 'quiet' admits.
thumbnailSurvival: Judged on the 120px sheets alone, the twelve mostly still read as twelve, and the silhouette families are what carries them: 9369 (disc plus satellite), 10443 (small diamond, lots of ground), 10264 (bright gold burst) and 9190 (square with a visible nested square) are unmistakable at browse size. Three failures. 9011, 10622 and 10980 converge into the same read -- brown mass with a gold fringe -- and can only be told apart by squinting at fringe placement. 10085 is close to an undifferentiated dark rectangle and loses its hexagon entirely. And on the states sheet at 120px, 9011 stress and 9548 stress are effectively the same image, a dull brown twelve-point star with nothing left to distinguish them, because the stress transform removed the very arms that were 9548's identity. So the collection survives thumbnailing on the seed axis but degrades on it under stress, which is the opposite of a brief that wanted the states to be the invisible part.
marketResponse: The change is unambiguously VISIBLE, and it is emphatically NOT the change that was claimed. This axis is where the work is judged against 'the market may register, but only faintly' and 'nothing that a casual viewer would notice at thumbnail size'. On holdout-states-120 the three rows separate without any tile-to-tile comparison: the stress row is uniformly smaller, dimmer and simplified, the recovery row uniformly larger, brighter and more ornate. It is not a 'slight tightening or loosening of the enclosure' -- it is three simultaneous transforms (scale contraction, desaturation toward flat brown, and wholesale removal of satellite structure) compounding in the same direction. 9548 goes from three arms to zero and back to more arms than it started with. 9369's disc shrinks to roughly half its neutral footprint. 9190's inner content contracts inside a square that stays put, which is the closest any tile comes to the commissioned behaviour and is the proof the restrained version was reachable. Delivering a spectacular market response is normally a virtue; here it is the specific thing the brief forbade in its last sentence.
tokenIdentity: Uneven, and the failures track exactly the seeds with satellite structure. 9190 holds across all three states -- the square, the nested inner square and the star fringe all persist and only their spacing and brightness move; that is the behaviour the brief describes. 9369 holds by a thread: the moon chain survives stress only as a single faint dot, but it is enough to name the token. 9011 holds, its twelve-point star surviving as the through-line. 9548 does not hold: neutral is an asymmetric three-armed budding form and stress is a bare symmetric twelve-point star with no arms, which is not the same object under drawdown but a different and much more generic one -- at 120px it is indistinguishable from 9011 stress. When the transform deletes the feature that made a token identifiable, the token has been replaced rather than affected, and that is one of four states-sheet seeds.
artifacts: No mush, no collisions that read as accidents, no vanished strokes, and the edges are clean vector boundaries throughout -- the rendering itself is sound. What I do see is frame handling. 10801's large square is cut by both the left and the bottom edges in a way that reads as mis-sized rather than as an intentional crop, and its interior square sits off-centre against a boundary that is not there. 10264's gold polygons are clipped at the right and bottom, 10980 is clipped at the top and right, and 9727's upper-left arm runs into the left edge. Against a brief that asks for 'most of the frame given to the dark' these are not neutral croppings, they are the composition overrunning its container. Separately, 10085's contrast against the ground is low enough to count as a defect at 120px, where it reads as a nearly empty tile. Finally the interiors are inert: in the majority of tokens the central region is one flat brown field with no incident, so there is nothing to reward the closer look that a 'contemplative object' invites.
reasoning: I refuse this, and the thing that decided it is the disagreement between my own blind description and the brief's last sentence. Before reading anything I wrote that the state change is large, one-directional, and readable at 120px with no need to compare tiles; the brief asks for a work that barely acknowledges the market, registers only faintly, would not be noticed at thumbnail size, and closes with 'Do not manufacture drama'. The market response is not merely stronger than commissioned, it is the single loudest fact about the sheets, and it is produced by three compounding transforms where the brief asked for one small one. The secondary failure supports it: the brief names the small dense centre and the count of enclosures as both the subject and the axis of variation, and in most tokens the centre is a large inert brown field while the real variation comes from radiating limbs that are not enclosures at all. This is not a refusal for being a different artwork than commissioned in the sense the instructions warn against -- the work is competent, coherent, and on-palette, and I would happily pass it against a brief that asked for a market-reactive emblem. It is a refusal because the one behaviour this brief explicitly and twice prohibited is the behaviour the work is built around, and briefFidelity is a gate.
wouldChange: Cut the state transform from three compounding axes to one. Hold hue, saturation and overall footprint constant across neutral, stress and recovery, and let the market move only the spacing between concentric boundaries -- a few percent of tightening or loosening, enough to reward a collector who lines up three states and invisible to anyone scrolling a grid. Never delete structure under stress: 9548 must keep its three arms in all three states, because they are what makes it 9548. Then invert the focal hierarchy to match the brief's own subject: put the density and the highest contrast in a genuinely small centre and let the outer enclosures be thin, quiet, low-alpha rings, rather than the current arrangement where the rim is bright and the middle is a flat inert mass. Make the count of those enclosures the primary seed variable, as the brief specifies, and demote the radiating limbs to a rare accent or drop them, since they are the feature pushing 9727 and 9906 out of the 'still and settled' register. Give every token a real margin so nothing clips (10801, 10264, 10980, 9727), and lift 10085's fills far enough off the ground to be visible at 120px.
